sources.entry: Jitsi Meet - WebRTC application that uses Jitsi Videobridge to provide high quality, scalable video conferences. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Nodejs/Docker/deb

summary.one_liner: Jitsi Meet is an open source, browser-based video conferencing application built on the Jitsi Videobridge, which can be used directly at meet.jit.si or self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Jitsi Meet as a set of open source projects for running video conferencing platforms with high video quality and features. It is browser-based, so participants can join from any current browser, and it also has mobile apps for Android (including F-Droid) and iOS. Listed features include HD audio and video, content sharing, raise hand and reactions, private chat, polls, and virtual backgrounds. The project provides Debian packages and a Docker setup for running your own instance, and advanced users can build all components from source. Web and native SDKs are offered for integration into other applications. The README also points to 8x8's paid hosted offering, Jitsi as a Service (JaaS), as an alternative to self-hosting.
use_cases: embedding video calls in an app via SDK
webinars with screen sharing and polls
private alternative to commercial video calls
how_to_run: Use the hosted service at meet.jit.si without installing anything
Install from Debian packages (see the handbook for instructions)
Deploy using the Docker setup described in the handbook
Build all components from source for advanced setups
notable: Supports Android, iOS, and web browsers, plus web and native SDKs for integration
Offers Debian packages and a Docker setup for self-hosting
Features include screen sharing, polls, virtual backgrounds, and private chat
Hosted version at meet.jit.si is free to use with a Google, Facebook, or GitHub account
caveats: Running your own instance requires setup through the handbook; the README does not detail hardware or scaling requirements
Monitoring, scaling, and updates are the operator's responsibility unless you use the paid JaaS service
Hosted JaaS is an enterprise offering from 8x8 and is separate from the open source project
